approach:
I read the requirement-steps procedure for REQ-05 and the two contracted inputs, the approved feat.brd and org.templates. I also read the source ticket file to confirm wording; the BRD already cites it. I then drafted feat.prd against the PRD template: summary, user stories, numbered acceptance criteria in EARS form, non-functional requirements and open questions. The PRD carries the BRD's scope, business rules, success measures, out-of-scope items, assumptions and open questions forward without adding scope. It also has a BRD-to-PRD traceability table and a validation check against the template, the BRD, the decision log and the approved lessons. An independent verifier subagent checked the draft. It found that AC-2 silently decided BRD question OQ-B6 (an unpaid row that has a paid_date) and that a few statements were unlabelled extrapolations. I fixed all of these:
- AC-2 now covers paid rows only.
- The "So that" clauses are marked as agent judgement.
- The end-to-end match criterion is now assumption P-A4.
- The PQ-1 and PQ-3 wording no longer goes beyond the sources.

judge.notes:
I checked the PRD against feat.brd (REQ-05 input), org.templates, requirements/ZD-48600.md, memory/MEMORY.md and the step brief.

Template: all five PRD template sections are present (summary, user stories, numbered EARS acceptance criteria, non-functional requirements, open questions). AC-1 to AC-23 all use the "When ..., the system shall ..." form. US-1 to US-5 use As a / I want / So that.

Carry-forward: every BRD item reaches the PRD unchanged.
- S-1 to S-7 and BR-1 to BR-16 each map to at least one acceptance criterion or NFR. I spot-checked BR-5/AC-8/AC-9 (strict thresholds), BR-7/AC-14 (exactly 30 days is not listed), BR-11/AC-17 ('unknown'), BR-13/BR-14 with AC-19 to AC-21, BR-15/AC-11 and BR-16/NFR-6.
- SM-1 to SM-5 are covered, and SM-6 is carried as OQ-B3.
- OS-1 to OS-8 are restated correctly.
- B-A1 to B-A7 match the BRD wording.
- OQ-B1 to OQ-B10 match the BRD, including the recorded owners: OQ-B1 is PM / Leadership and OQ-B5 is PM.

Numbers and identifiers match their sources: 30/10 thresholds, the 30-day boundary, 60-day REG-LPR-2026-4.2, 02:00 Asia/Kolkata, Python 3.9 / Node.js 22, 2026-10-24, T2, R-AP-12, R-AP-14, PROV-ACME-2026-11, feed v3/v2, ZD-48470/48501/48211, and D-2026-031/044/050 with L-007/L-011.

Assumptions: the PRD's new interpretations are labelled as agent judgement or new assumptions and sent to the gate (PQ-2). They are:
- P-A1: `days` counts from due_date to as_of.
- P-A2: the id tie-break is ascending, compared as text.
- P-A3: the meaning of an invalid paid_date.
- P-A4: what the end-to-end test checks.
- The purposes in US-2 to US-5 and the PM as actor in US-5.
- NFR-3, which applies D-2026-044 to ap_portal.

Open questions: OQ-B6 is deliberately left unresolved. AC-2 is limited to paid rows so that it does not decide that case. The new questions PQ-1 to PQ-6 are real gaps: the empty-history edge case, the JSON contract and the type of `days`, NFR targets, ordering against PROV-ACME-2026-11, and feed v3 availability.

Validation check: present and accurate. It covers the template, carry-forward, the decision log and lessons applied, and finds no conflicts.

The only weak point is the "Runtimes are unchanged" wording in NFR-10, which no source states as a requirement. No test or CI results are claimed, so there was nothing to check against tool views.
